bf16.note: The original arm's long extension-versus-fresh guard exceeded the unchanged 0.00001 tolerance. All recorded A/B hidden/output phase hashes match. This does not establish a complete BF16 timing result.

limitations: The Q8 catalog is exploratory, not a causal before/after comparison.
GPU timestamps and unprofiled wall times come from separate runs. Profiling alters passes and optional paths. Their difference is not measured CPU time.
Kernel shares use the sum of label medians, not wall time. Optional Gemma labels were dispatched in only some samples.
The host was contended. Earlier agent-owned builds overlapped parts of this campaign. Serialization of GPU writers did not eliminate CPU interference.
Laya and Clef expose rounded public outputs. Other models expose raw distributions. Agreement is not a task-accuracy evaluation.
BF16 stopped at an unchanged numerical guard in the original arm. Partial timing rows are not a complete performance campaign.
WASM memory byteLength is a committed high-water size. It does not measure live residual allocation or transient peak.
No universal fastest-kernel, whole-catalog improvement, camera-throughput or foreground-responsiveness claim is made.
